api_quick_reference.signature: fit_local_level_step(predictor: np.ndarray, values: np.ndarray, splits: np.ndarray, *, scale: float, loss_clip: float) -> tuple[int, float]
api_quick_reference.doc_summary: Fit finite predictor and values (n,) and integer splits (k,) with k >= 1, at least three samples per side, full-rank split designs, and positive scale and loss clip, returning (best split index, signed level change).

mathematical_preconditions: Inputs are finite real arrays convertible to float64, with magnitudes that keep intermediate residuals, model evaluations, and least-squares calculations representable. The linear fit requires a nonempty (n,p) design and an (n,) response with n >= p >= 1 and numerical full column rank, including after Cauchy row weighting. Supplied scale and noise_floor must be positive finite scalars.

The relaxation fit requires aligned length-n vectors, n >= 4, strictly increasing nonnegative times measured from the supplied onset, and a predictor numerically independent of the intercept. The onset rate is independently specified and nonnegative, noise_scale is positive, curvature_ratio is nonnegative, 2 <= bins <= n, and 0 < tau_min < tau_max. The saturation branch requires a positive onset rate, a numerically full-rank fitted Jacobian, and a positive slope not active at its lower bound.

The step fit requires aligned length-n vectors and a nonempty integer vector of candidate split indices, each leaving at least three samples on either side. Each candidate design must have full column rank: the predictor cannot be constant within both segments. The scale and loss_clip are positive finite scalars. Interpretation as a level step assumes a shared local trend on both sides.

staged_wormhole_modules.exported_apis: def align_reference_panel(values: np.ndarray, controls: np.ndarray, groups: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray; def balanced_cell_weights(groups: np.ndarray, strata: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray; def weighted_column_fill(values: np.ndarray, weights: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray

api_quick_reference.signature: align_reference_panel(values: np.ndarray, controls: np.ndarray, groups: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray
api_quick_reference.doc_summary: Return aligned real values (n, p) using real controls (n, q) and finite real groups (n,), with nonempty columns and a supported positive control gain per group.
Return positive mean-one weights (n,) from nonempty finite real vectors groups (n,) and strata (n,) with every observed group–stratum combination present.
Return finite-entry weighted means (p,) for a nonempty real matrix values (n, p) with finite positive weights (n,), using zero for unobserved columns.

mathematical_preconditions: Alignment accepts real numeric arrays of shapes (n, p) and (n, q), with p, q > 0, and a finite real group vector of shape (n,). Nonfinite panel entries are treated as missing. Each group must have at least one control with two finite observations, a finite median control mean, and a finite, strictly positive median control population standard deviation. A constant control can contribute; a zero median gain raises ValueError.

Interpreting alignment as removal of a nuisance transform assumes a shared additive offset and positive multiplicative gain for signals and controls within each group. The control panel must have comparable baseline location and spread across groups, independent of sample composition. These scientific assumptions cannot be verified by shape or moment checks.

Cell weighting requires two nonempty, finite real vectors of matching shape (n,). Every combination of an observed group and an observed stratum must be present. If there are K such cells, each row in a cell of size m receives weight n/(K*m).

Column fill requires a nonempty real matrix of shape (n, p) and finite, strictly positive row weights of shape (n,). Nonfinite entries are excluded from both numerator and denominator; a column with no finite observations returns zero. Numeric panel and fill arithmetic use float64 and assume intermediate sums, squares, and ratios are within usable float64 range.
